full_name: Center for Security and Emerging Technology
mission: CSET is a Georgetown University policy research centre that studies how AI, advanced computing and biotechnology affect national security. It combines analysts with a data-science team (around 60 analysis-ready datasets) and translates important Chinese-language AI documents, aiming to give US and allied policymakers non-partisan, evidence-based advice.

key_work.title: CSET publications library (AI governance, red-teaming, compute supply chains)
key_work.plain_summary: CSET's catalogue of reports, data briefs and translations on AI and national security — the main way its work reaches policymakers.

key_work.title: Emerging Technology Observatory
key_work.plain_summary: A CSET initiative that turns its large research datasets into public tools, so others can see where AI research and talent are growing.

key_work.title: Chinese-language document translations
key_work.plain_summary: English translations of significant Chinese AI policy and strategy documents, so Western readers can see what Chinese officials actually wrote.

status_note: part of Georgetown University's Walsh School of Foreign Service; Helen Toner listed as Executive Director (Oct 2026)
status_raw: active — part of Georgetown University's Walsh School of Foreign Service; Helen Toner listed as Executive Director (Oct 2026)

warnings.text: AI is reshaping national security and US–China competition, and policymakers often lack reliable data about it.
Powerful AI systems can be misused (e.g. cyber attacks, disinformation) and need testing such as red-teaming before deployment.
AI progress is outpacing safeguards (Helen Toner, 2026 interviews).

recommendations.text: Base AI policy on rigorous, data-driven analysis rather than hype.
Strengthen AI red-teaming and evaluation practices.
Prepare a new generation of decision-makers who understand emerging technology.
